title: TabPrep: Closing the Feature Engineering Gap in Tabular Benchmarks
claim: Model-centric advances rarely beat the previous best, while simple data-centric feature engineering sets new peak performance on most datasets.
layout: 1 wide scatter panel, datasets sorted left-to-right, shaded gap region and stars
description: A single wide scatter plot with datasets on the x-axis, in rotated labels, sorted by the gain from TabPrep. The y-axis is a symmetric-log relative improvement over the previous best, running from more than 5% worse to more than 50% better. A dotted horizontal line marks the previous best on TabArena. A legend across the top lists models by color with counts: TabPFN-2.6 (blue) and TabICLv2 (orange) are the model-centric baselines. The green-boxed TabPrep group has brown, red, pink and purple variants. A green line traces the best result per dataset and rises to the right. The region under it is shaded light green and labeled 'Feature engineering gap'. Stars mark new peak performance. TabPrep stars dominate the right side. The eye goes to the rising green curve and the stars.
caption: Illustration of how TabPrep exposes the peak performance gap missed by models. We zoom into the top of the leaderboard per dataset on the TabArena benchmark and compare recent model-centric improvements (TabPFN-2.6 [ref], TabICLv2 [ref]) along with our data-centric improvements from augmenting four models with TabPrep. Improvement is relative to the previous best out of 25 TabArena models tuned for 200 configurations, including the non-TabPrep-augmented versions of the models. The y-axis is on a symmetric log scale. Datasets are ordered by the highest gain from TabPrep. Improvement is averaged over folds. Numbers in the legend correspond to the number of datasets where a model improves peak performance. Stars mark new peak performance.
abstract: Progress in tabular machine learning has largely focused on increasingly sophisticated model architectures. At the same time, feature engineering remains a critical yet underexplored component of real-world modeling pipelines that is entirely absent from modern benchmarks, which creates an unquantified evaluation gap. In this work, we introduce TabPrep, a lightweight preprocessing pipeline composed of feature generators that are carefully designed to target three specific structural data patterns. We show that many widely used model classes exhibit predictable blind spots to these patterns and that systematic feature engineering alone can establish new peak performance. Across the TabArena benchmark, integrating TabPrep into model training and tuning consistently improves performance for tree-based, neural, linear, and foundation models, often surpassing gains achieved by model-centric innovations alone. TabPrep outperforms previous automated feature engineering approaches in performance, efficiency, and applicability across datasets, enabling integration into large-scale benchmarks. By releasing TabPrep (see https://github.com/atschalz/tabprep), we enable researchers to integrate feature engineering into their benchmarking setup, filling a longstanding gap in tabular evaluations.
